title: Protect PDF – Add a Password to a PDF Free, No Upload
description: Password-protect a PDF in your browser with AES-256 encryption, and choose whether people may print, copy or change it. Free, nothing is uploaded.
heading: Protect PDF
subtitle: Lock a PDF with a password and AES-256 encryption, and decide what people may do with it; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Add a password to a PDF online without sending it anywhere: the file is encrypted with AES-256 right in your browser. Anyone who opens the copy needs the password, and you can ask PDF readers to block printing, copying or changes. Your file and your password never leave your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your file and your password are handled by your own browser and never sent to a server.

features.title: Strong encryption
features.text: AES-256, the strongest encryption PDF readers support, applied in your browser.

features.title: Permissions
features.text: Allow or block printing, copying text and pictures, and changes.

steps.title: Choose your PDF
steps.text: Click Choose a file, or drop a PDF on the page.

steps.title: Type a password
steps.text: Type it twice; choose one you can remember, because it can't be recovered.

steps.title: Choose the permissions
steps.text: Untick what people may not do once it's open: print, copy or change it.

steps.title: Protect and download
steps.text: Click Protect PDF and download the locked copy.

handles: AES-256 encryption with a password to open.
Printing, copying and changes allowed or blocked, with a permissions password.
Any PDF that opens without a password, including one that only restricts printing or copying; text, pictures, links and form fields stay as they are.
limits: A forgotten password can't be recovered, here or anywhere else.
Permissions are honoured by PDF readers; they are not a lock on what someone who can open the file sees.
A PDF that already needs a password to open must be unlocked first. Printing or copying restrictions already on a file are replaced by the ones you choose.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your file is read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: How strong is the protection?
faq.answer: The copy is encrypted with AES-256, the strongest encryption PDF readers support. Its strength depends on the password: use a long one.

faq.question: What if I forget the password?
faq.answer: It can't be recovered. Keep the original file, which stays unchanged on your device.

faq.question: What is the permissions password for?
faq.answer: It lets a PDF reader allow printing, copying and changes again. The restrictions are honoured by most readers, but they are not a lock: anyone who has the password to open the file can remove them, for example with Unlock PDF. Only the password to open keeps the file private.

faq.question: How do I remove the password later?
faq.answer: With Unlock PDF and the password.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.

faq.question: How do I put a password on a PDF?
faq.answer: Encrypt the PDF with a password, so anyone who opens it must type the password first; Preview on a Mac can do it when exporting. OpenAnyDoc's Protect PDF does it in your browser with AES-256: choose the PDF, type the password twice and download the locked copy, and neither the file nor the password is uploaded.
